solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Distressed husband inquires about Liberal surrender

indicators.note: something distressed has been knocked about and damaged, so its letters are out of shape

explanation.surface: A worried husband asks whether a Liberal politician is about to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks you to read inquires as a verb; it is only a bag of letters for the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: both words mean to give something up or hand it over.

clue.text: Express first to run article on slump being over

indicators.note: the first of the word run is its opening letter
something over has been turned over, and in a down clue that sends the word upwards

parts.note: a dip = a slump, here written upwards

explanation.surface: A market report: an express train running into a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: Express looks like a verb or a train; it is the adjective, as in express delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: an express train or delivery is a fast one.

clue.text: Reconstruction of US–Italian boat that sank

indicators.note: reconstructing something rebuilds it in a new form, so the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A joint US–Italian project to rebuild a famous wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lusitania was the British liner torpedoed in 1915 with many Americans aboard, so the US link is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the Cunard liner sunk by a U-boat off Ireland in 1915.

clue.text: Press here for further information?

parts.note: the surface pushes a button to push; the setter means the press, journalists, gathered here
not a help link but reporters there to get more facts

explanation.surface: An instruction on a web page or device: press this button to learn more.
explanation.walkthrough: Press is the gathered journalists, not a button, and they are here to extract further information.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists, collectively the press, gather at such an event to be told more.

clue.text: State of university weightlifter announced

indicators.note: something announced is said out loud, so we want the sound of the word

explanation.surface: A national team's student weightlifter being named.
explanation.walkthrough: The weightlifter is a machine, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an Eastern European country is a state.

clue.text: Hidden meaning of message from Times staffer?

explanation.surface: Reading between the lines of a note from someone at The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a sub is just one example of a Times staffer; this puzzle is in The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: what lies beneath the literal words of a text is its hidden meaning.

clue.text: City's first to abandon support for Bank of Scotland

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it

explanation.surface: The City of London withdrawing support for the Bank of Scotland in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: Bank of Scotland reads as the lender; it is a Scottish bank of earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional use: brae is the Scots word for a hillside or steep bank.

clue.text: Contact that woman about checking account

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, as in about-face
checking something holds it back

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with a woman about her checking account.
explanation.walkthrough: Checking account suggests banking; checking here means restraining.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to get hold of someone by phone or letter is to get through to them.

clue.text: Sociable former leftie welcoming vicar from down under

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from under means reading from the bottom up

explanation.surface: A friendly ex-Trotskyist hosting a vicar from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: From down under suggests Australia; in a down clue it means upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: outgoing people who love company are sociable.

clue.text: This won't end well, as undertaker might put it

definitions.meaning: the idiom warning someone that the bad consequences are theirs
taken literally, what an undertaker could say to a client

explanation.surface: A warning that things will go badly, in an undertaker's phrasing.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom warns someone that the consequences are theirs; an undertaker could say it literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase tells someone their rash choice will rebound on them, and it is also literally an undertaker's line.

clue.text: Naval officer celebrated defending west following hostilities

indicators.note: to defend something is to surround and protect it

parts.note: a star is celebrated, split round W

explanation.surface: A famous naval officer holding the western front after the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Celebrated reads as a verb of partying; it is the adjective famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin prefix: post means after, so the word names the period once fighting has ended.

clue.text: Constituent's got teeth into first minor role

indicators.note: first says which word comes at the front

parts.note: a part is a constituent; the ’s is 'has'

explanation.surface: A voter who has sunk their teeth into a small first job.
explanation.walkthrough: Constituent reads as a voter; it is a component, and constituent’s means constituent has.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre term: a small acting part with few lines.

clue.text: Time to replace female in flawed investigative role

indicators.note: to replace something is to take its place

explanation.surface: A plea to recast a poorly written female detective part.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures casting a TV role; the swap is one letter inside a word meaning flawed.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the part in a whodunit whose job is to investigate.

clue.text: Lout rounds on upper-class Brit

indicators.note: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B, so the rounds come after the Brit

parts.note: a yah is a posh Brit, from their way of saying yes

explanation.surface: A thug going for a posh British man.
explanation.walkthrough: Rounds on reads as attacks, the lout turning on the toff; it is a placement instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary origin: Swift's brutish Yahoos in Gulliver's Travels gave the word for a coarse lout.

clue.text: Man of the cloth shot at table, I hear

indicators.note: what I hear is the sound, not the spelling

parts.note: a cannon is a billiards shot striking two balls

explanation.surface: A priest playing a shot at the billiard table.
explanation.walkthrough: The table is a billiards or snooker table, where a cannon is a shot hitting two balls in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a cathedral clergyman is one kind of man of the cloth.

clue.text: Falls that may affect your vision?

explanation.surface: A question whether waterfalls can spoil your view.
explanation.walkthrough: Falls reads as tumbles; it is waterfalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: great waterfalls, and the eye condition that clouds the lens.

clue.text: Hangers-on left without whiskey today

parts.note: whiskey is W in the phonetic alphabet, removed

explanation.surface: Groupies going home dry these days.
explanation.walkthrough: Whiskey is the NATO alphabet's W, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective noun: the followers around a celebrity, the hangers-on.

clue.text: Biography of a setter? It's not much fun

definitions.meaning: a setter is a gun dog, and its biography is its life
the idiom for a miserable existence

explanation.surface: A crossword setter's life story, dismissed as dull.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the dog breed, not the crossword compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a wretched, put-upon existence, and literally the life of a dog such as a setter.

clue.text: Election official hosting party briefly — she's off to foreign parts

definitions.note: The definition is a clause describing the answer: a person heading abroad.

indicators.note: said briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes
a host has guests inside the house

parts.note: a teller counts votes, split round RAV

explanation.surface: A vote counter throwing a quick party before leaving the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash splits wordplay from a definition that is a whole clause, describing the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: someone going abroad is making a journey.

clue.text: Raised current trouble with offspring's affair

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted up means written upwards

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A parent angry about a child's romance.
explanation.walkthrough: Raised sounds like anger at the affair; it only lifts the first two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a secret romantic relationship, an affair.

clue.text: It's dependent on soldier getting hold of £1

indicators.note: to get hold of something is to grasp it

parts.note: L for pound, I for one

explanation.surface: A soldier's pay packet: surviving on a single pound.
explanation.walkthrough: Dependent on looks like one phrase; on belongs to the wordplay as RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: leaning on something else for support.

clue.text: Ignore fool on vacation abroad

indicators.note: a vacated place has been emptied, so fool loses its middle

explanation.surface: Advice to pay no attention to an idiot on holiday overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: On vacation means a holiday; here it empties fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to disregard a rule openly and with contempt.

clue.text: Earlier I fled, carrying weapon

indicators.note: something carrying a load holds it inside, as these words hold the answer

explanation.surface: A confession of escaping while armed.
explanation.walkthrough: Carrying reads as bearing arms, which suits the surface, but it is the hiding instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a long-barrelled gun is one kind of weapon.

clue.text: Enemy capturing retreating king's army

indicators.note: to capture is to take prisoner and hold
a retreating army goes backwards, so CR is written backwards

parts.note: a foe is an enemy, split round RC

explanation.surface: An enemy seizing a defeated king's troops.
explanation.walkthrough: CR stands for Carolus Rex, King Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a body of troops, as in armed forces.

clue.text: Pull Danes out completely

indicators.note: out can mean out of order or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An order to haul the Danes out entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: Out completely looks like one phrase; out is the anagram signal and completely stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to beat someone all ends up is to beat them thoroughly.

clue.text: Wine producer's drink? There's nothing in it

indicators.note: something in it sits inside it

explanation.surface: A vintner's glass turns out to be empty.
explanation.walkthrough: The producer is the grape, not the winemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword stretch: the Pinot grape varieties produce wines such as Pinot Noir.

clue.text: Accra poorly placed as capital

indicators.note: letters poorly placed are in the wrong positions and need moving

explanation.surface: A verdict that Accra is badly sited to be a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Accra, capital of Ghana, is only fodder; the answer is another capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Venezuelan seat of government is one capital city.

clue.text: A right lot of wets reportedly in charge

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a spelling that sounds like rain

parts.note: rain is a lot of wet

explanation.surface: A bunch of feeble moderates running things.
explanation.walkthrough: Wets are weak Tory moderates in British politics; here the wet stuff is rain. In charge looks like one phrase, but in is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal sense: to call someone before a court to answer a formal accusation.

clue.text: Goes back to well

indicators.note: going back means going the reverse way, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: goes = pees, as in goes to the toilet

explanation.walkthrough: Well is the verb, as in tears welling up.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: liquid that wells up oozes slowly out.

clue.text: Final part of scene omitted from terribly sentimental episode

indicators.note: the final part of a word is its last letter
something omitted is left out, so that letter leaves the word
something done terribly is done badly, so the remaining letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Cutting the last bit of a scene from a mawkish soap episode.
explanation.walkthrough: SENTIMENTAL has two Es; losing either leaves the same ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: one part of a serial broadcast or published in parts.
